subject: anaesthesia
title: Physiological Monitoring: Pulse Oximetry, Capnography, and Arterial Waveforms

steps.title: Beer-Lambert Law and Dual Wavelengths
steps.tx: **Pulse oximetry optical principles** combine spectrophotometry and plethysmography based on the Beer-Lambert law. The probe emits two specific light wavelengths through pulsating arteriolar tissue: red light at 660 nanometers, preferentially absorbed by deoxygenated haemoglobin, and infrared light at 940 nanometers, preferentially absorbed by oxygenated haemoglobin. The ratio of pulsatile (AC) to non-pulsatile background (DC) absorption calculates arterial oxygen saturation.
steps.say: Pulse oximetry optical principles combine spectrophotometry and plethysmography based on the Beer-Lambert law. The probe emits two specific light wavelengths through pulsating arteriolar tissue: red light at 660 nanometers, preferentially absorbed by deoxygenated haemoglobin, and infrared light at 940 nanometers, preferentially absorbed by oxygenated haemoglobin. The ratio of pulsatile (AC) to non-pulsatile background (DC) absorption calculates arterial oxygen saturation.

rows: Predominant absorption at normal high saturation
Equal absorption by OxyHb and DeoxyHb
Used as optical reference calibration wavelength

steps.title: Pulse Oximetry Dyshaemoglobinaemias
steps.tx: **Dyshaemoglobinaemia optical artefacts** severely mislead pulse oximetry readings: carboxyhaemoglobin absorbs light identically to oxyhaemoglobin at 660 nanometers, falsely elevating SpO2 to near 100 percent despite lethal tissue hypoxia. Methaemoglobin absorbs equally at both 660 and 940 nanometers, locking the calculated R ratio to 1.0, which forces pulse oximeters to falsely display an SpO2 of 85 percent regardless of true arterial oxygenation.

Methaemoglobin absorbs equally at both 660 and 940 nanometers, locking the calculated R ratio to 1.0, which forces pulse oximeters to falsely display an SpO2 of 85 percent regardless of true arterial oxygenation.

left.title: Carboxyhaemoglobinemia (CO Poisoning)
points: Absorbs 660 nm red light identically to oxyhaemoglobin
Pulse oximeter displays falsely reassuring 98 to 100 percent SpO2
Diagnosed accurately only with laboratory co-oximetry

right.title: Methaemoglobinaemia (Fe3+ Oxidation)
points: Equal absorption at both 660 nm and 940 nm wavelengths
Refractory fixed reading of 85 percent regardless of PaO2
Treated emergently with intravenous methylene blue (1-2 mg/kg)

steps.title: Capnography Waveform Phases
steps.tx: **Capnogram waveform morphology** plots exhaled carbon dioxide partial pressure against time across four physiological phases: Phase I represents carbon dioxide-free gas clearing anatomical dead space; Phase II is the steep S-shaped upstroke mixing dead space with alveolar gas; Phase III is the horizontal alveolar plateau representing pure alveolar gas; and Phase 0 is the rapid vertical inspiratory downstroke.

rows: Exhalation of anatomical conducting dead space
Baseline elevation indicates rebreathing or faulty valve
Transition from dead space to alveolar gas mixing
Slanted delayed upstroke in obstructive airway disease
Emptying of true alveolar gas across all lung units
Shark-fin upward slope in acute bronchospasm
Rapid inhalation of fresh CO2-free gas
Slurred prolonged downstroke in inspiratory valve incompetence

steps.title: EtCO2 to PaCO2 Gradient
steps.tx: **Alveolar-arterial carbon dioxide gradient** reflects ventilation-perfusion matching in the lungs: under normal anaesthetized conditions, end-tidal carbon dioxide (EtCO2) is 35 to 45 mmHg, which is 2 to 5 mmHg lower than arterial carbon dioxide (PaCO2) due to normal physiological alveolar dead space. Any increase in dead space, such as massive pulmonary embolism or profound haemorrhagic shock, widens this gradient dramatically.

left.title: Normal Gradient (2 to 5 mmHg)
points: Homogeneous pulmonary perfusion and ventilation matching
EtCO2 reliably tracks systemic arterial carbon dioxide tension
Minimal alveolar dead space ventilation in healthy lungs

right.title: Widened Gradient (greater than 10 mmHg)
points: Massive pulmonary thromboembolism or gas embolism
Profound hemorrhagic shock and systemic hypoperfusion
Ventilated alveoli lose pulmonary capillary blood flow

steps.title: Diagnostic Capnography Patterns
steps.tx: **Diagnostic capnogram patterns** instantly reveal acute life-threatening anaesthetic emergencies: a sudden catastrophic loss of EtCO2 to zero indicates circuit disconnection, total endotracheal tube extubation, or cardiac arrest with circulatory standstill. A continuous upward sloping Phase III (shark-fin appearance) with an increased alpha angle signifies acute bronchospasm or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, responding to bronchodilators.

nodes.label: Sudden drop of EtCO2 to flatline zero
Check chest rise, breath sounds, and pulse
Rule out circuit disconnect or esophageal tube

steps.title: ECG Lead Selection and Ischaemia
steps.tx: **Intraoperative electrocardiographic lead selection** balances rhythm surveillance against myocardial ischaemia detection: Lead II aligns closely with the electrical axis of atrial depolarization, displaying the largest P waves to identify dysrhythmias and junctional rhythms. Meanwhile, precordial Lead V5, positioned at the fifth intercostal space along the anterior axillary line, detects up to 75 percent of left ventricular subendocardial ischaemic ST-segment depressions.

rows: Right arm to left leg vector
Detects approximately 75 percent of ischaemic episodes
Detects greater than 80 to 90 percent of ischaemic events
Adjunctive lead for multi-vessel coronary disease

steps.title: Invasive Arterial Blood Pressure Monitoring
steps.tx: **Invasive arterial pressure waveform monitoring** provides continuous beat-to-beat pressure measurement and vascular stroke volume assessment via radial artery cannulation. The transduced waveform exhibits a sharp systolic upstroke, systolic peak pressure, and a dicrotic notch reflecting aortic valve closure. Overdamped systems falsely underestimate systolic pressure and overestimate diastolic pressure, while underdamped systems produce exaggerated systolic overshoot from resonance resonance.

left.title: Overdamped Arterial Trace
points: Air bubbles, blood clots, or compliant soft tubing
Slurred upstroke with absent dicrotic notch
Falsely low systolic and falsely high diastolic pressure

right.title: Underdamped Arterial Trace
points: Excessive tubing length or multiple stopcocks
Exaggerated systolic spiking and ringing vibrations
Falsely elevated systolic and falsely low diastolic pressure

steps.title: Central Venous Pressure Waveforms
steps.tx: **Central venous pressure waveform analysis** reflects right atrial pressure fluctuations across the cardiac cycle: the 'a' wave represents end-diastolic right atrial contraction; the 'c' wave marks early systolic tricuspid valve closure bulging into the atrium; the 'v' wave reflects systolic right atrial filling against a closed tricuspid valve; the 'x' descent represents atrial relaxation; and the 'y' descent marks diastolic ventricular filling after tricuspid opening.

nodes.label: Ventricular systole causes c wave and x descent
Atrial venous filling creates v wave
Tricuspid valve opening produces y descent
